subject: Day 51: confirm daycare overlap
bodyText:
Today's focus
At 51 days, the survival phase is giving way to operational planning. Today's priority is locking the childcare transition so the handoff has a buffer rather than a hard cutover.

Action items
- Confirm the daycare or nanny start date with a 3-5 day overlap with the primary caregiver, so the handoff is supervised rather than abrupt. ChildCare.gov: https://www.childcare.gov/
- Draft the caregiver onboarding packet now: pediatrician contact, feeding schedule, sleep cues, and emergency contacts, so it is ready before day one.
- Schedule the 2-month well visit if it is not yet booked; the rotavirus first dose must be given by about day 104, so do not let the visit drift past day 70. AAP periodicity schedule: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/care-delivery-approaches/periodicity-schedule/

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Early drool from salivary-gland maturation, not teething; first teeth typically arrive at 6-10 months.
- [monitor] A persistent head tilt to one side with limited rotation (torticollis), common after in-utero positioning; flag it at the 2-month visit for a possible PT referral.
- [call within 24h] Inconsolable crying that pairs with poor feeding and decreased output, or a new bluish tint to the lips during feeds.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C) under 90 days, apnea, or color change demands a same-day call or 911 right away!

Enrichment opportunities
- Encourage chest-off-the-floor push-ups on the forearms during tummy time; insufficient prone time is linked to small delays in rolling and sitting. HealthyChildren tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Take a 20-30 minute daylight stroller loop most days for varied sensory input and your own cardiovascular recovery; still give 400 IU/day of vitamin D since sun exposure does not replace the supplement for breastfed infants. HealthyChildren on vitamin D: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/healthy-living/nutrition/Pages/Vitamin-D-On-the-Double.aspx
- Respond to each coo as if it were a full sentence, then pause for his turn; these serve-and-return exchanges predict later language outcomes. Romeo et al. 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/

Upcoming
- Day 56-70: 2-month well visit; vaccines HepB #2, RV #1, DTaP #1, Hib #1, PCV #1, IPV #1.
- Day 57-72: post-vaccine 24-48h window of fussiness, low-grade fever, and extra sleep.
- Day 112-126: 4-month well visit; vaccines RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete

- Holds head up while on tummy
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained head lift of several seconds, not just a brief bob. Forearms may or may not be supporting yet.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-head-up-tummy/complete

- Hands relax open most of the time
  AAP window: day 35-90
  What to look for: Newborn fists relax as the palmar grasp reflex fades. Predictor of voluntary grasp coming.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/hands-open-mostly/complete

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete
